en.title: Jesus Saves
en.author: Priscilla J. Owens
stanzas:
[G]We have heard the joyful sound:
Jesus saves! Jesus [D]saves!
[D7]Spread the [G]tidings all around:
Jesus [D]saves! [D7]Jesus [G]saves!
[C]Bear the news to every land,
[G]Climb the steeps and cross the [D]waves;
Onward! [G]'tis our [C]Lord's command;
[G]Jesus [D]saves! [D7]Jesus [G]saves!

Waft it on the rolling tide:
Jesus saves! Jesus saves!
Tell to sinners far and wide:
Jesus saves! Jesus saves!
Sing, ye islands of the sea;
Echo back, ye ocean caves;
Earth shall keep her jubilee:
Jesus saves! Jesus saves!

Sing above the battle strife:
Jesus saves! Jesus saves!
By His death and endless life
Jesus saves! Jesus saves!
Sing it softly through the gloom,
When the heart for mercy craves;
Sing in triumph o'er the tomb:
Jesus saves! Jesus saves!

Give the winds a mighty voice:
Jesus saves! Jesus saves!
Let the nations now rejoice:
Jesus saves! Jesus saves!
Shout salvation full and free;
Highest hills and deepest caves;
This our song of victory:
Jesus saves! Jesus saves!

notes: Text: Timeless Truths' layout and punctuation (Hymnal of the Church of God 1953), with three readings restored to Owens' 1882 wording as hymnary's representative text (Our Great Redeemer's Praise #556) has them: 'Climb the steeps and cross the waves' (TT: 'Climb the mountains, cross the waves'), 'Sing, ye islands of the sea; Echo back, ye ocean caves' (TT: 'you'), and 'Sing it softly through the gloom' (TT: 'Shout it brightly through the gloom'). The Church of God readings are that book's alterations; the originals are what the hymnals this book serves print. Four stanzas in both. Tune JESUS SAVES (William J. Kirkpatrick, 1882), meter 7.6.7.6.7.7.7.6. Key G: hymnary's instances run 46 G to 7 F; TT prints G, already a guitar key. Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat. 'We have heard the joyful sound' is I with a IV6 neighbour (dropped); the first 'Jesus saves! Jesus saves!' ends on V, the second V-V7-I; 'Bear the news' is IV, 'Climb the steeps' I to V; 'Onward! 'tis our Lord's command' walks the bass G-F-E-D-C under I-I7-IV-I-IV, written as I to IV; the close V-V7-I.
